replies: Saved: Knows SQL, Excel and Tableau and did 2 years of reporting. Is that right?

Your SQL, Excel and Tableau skills map directly to core data-analyst needs.

Short answer: these fit — SQL, Excel, Tableau, plus "2 years of reporting" as practical experience.
Why each matters (one line each)
- SQL — essential for extracting and joining data, building datasets and performing most analyses. Employers expect it as baseline.
- Excel — needed for ad-hoc analysis, cleaning small datasets, pivot tables and quick modeling; common in teams that mix code and spreadsheets.
- Tableau — shows you can build dashboards and visualizations to present insights to stakeholders.
- 2 years of reporting — demonstrates recurring delivery, familiarity with business metrics and working with stakeholders; it’s evidence you turned data into decisions.
Gaps to add or highlight for stronger data-analyst matches
- Data cleaning/ETL skills (e.g., Python/pandas, SQL window functions, data pipelines).
- Statistical or analytical methods (A/B testing, regression, forecasting) and how you used them.
- Domain or metric examples (what you reported on: finance, marketing, ops, product).
- Impact numbers (e.g., reduced reporting time by X%, improved a metric by Y points).
- Other tools (Looker, Power BI, BigQuery, Git, Airflow) if you have them.
One next step: confirm the saved skill fact so I can use it when searching and tailoring applications, or tell me which domain you reported on (finance, marketing, operations, etc.). Is the saved skill line correct?
